def _strip_html(text):
    return BeautifulSoup(text, 'html.parser').get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)

def _is_html(text):
    return bool(re.search(r'<[a-zA-Z][^>]*>', text))

def _render(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        v = v.strip()
        if not v:

        return _strip_html(v) if _is_html(v) else v

print(repr(result_plain[:400]))

The real issue is that `_strip_html` uses `get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)` which only inserts `\n` between text nodes — heavily nested inline HTML (all the `<span style=...>` elements wrapping text with no block-level boundaries) produces zero line breaks. Let me read the full current `_strip_html` and `_render`:  

The two bugs share a root cause:

1. **`_strip_html`** uses `get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)` which only inserts `\n` between text nodes. HTML with deep `<span>` nesting but no block elements produces zero line breaks — a 6000-char wall of text.
2. **`_is_html` gate in `_render`**: if HTML slips past that check (or is stored in an old session before this code existed), `marked.parse` escapes `<` → `&lt;` by default in v17, displaying raw tags as visible text.

Two targeted fixes:
- **Backend**: rewrite `_strip_html` to insert `\n` at block elements before stripping, and remove the `_is_html` gate (BS4 returns plain text unchanged, so always calling it is safe)
- **Frontend**: detect raw HTML in `_renderJobText` and render via DOMPurify directly (fixes existing stored sessions)

function _renderJobText(text) {
  const raw = marked.parse(text, { gfm: true, breaks: true });
  return DOMPurify.sanitize(raw);
}
```

- oldString:

```
// Render job description text safely. If the text contains raw HTML (e.g. from
// sessions stored before server-side HTML stripping was added), sanitize and
// render it directly via DOMPurify. Otherwise parse as GFM markdown so that
// plain-text line breaks (\n) become visible breaks with breaks:true.
function _renderJobText(text) {
  if (/<[a-zA-Z][^>]*>/.test(text)) {
    return DOMPurify.sanitize(text);
  }
  const raw = marked.parse(text, { gfm: true, breaks: true });
  return DOMPurify.sanitize(raw);
}
```

**Frontend `job-input.js`** — reverted  to always use  first. My earlier HTML-detection regex `/<[a-zA-Z][^>]*>/` was matching GFM autolinks like `<https://...>` in the MarkItDown output, causing the entire text to be sent directly to DOMPurify. DOMPurify doesn't parse markdown, so  collapses to spaces and  / `**bold**` show as literal characters.  handles both markdown and embedded HTML correctly — GFM autolinks and inline HTML all pass through properly, and DOMPurify sanitizes the rendered output.

**Backend `job_routes.py`** — added deduplication before the section-building loop. Sites like UCB emit 4–5 identical empty `WebPage` JSON-LD scripts (SEO/navigation metadata with no job content).
